title: Reach the Browser Agent, and Say What It Can Do
description:
A browser agent could not discover or call this app's tools, and the page could not say why. Three defects stacked: the binding read navigator.modelContext when the browser keeps it on document.modelContext; the descriptors carried live Zod schemas across an agent boundary that only accepts structured-cloneable JSON Schema; and every resulting failure was swallowed by a bare catch. The page reported 'Agent attached - 9 tools' while registering none of them. The fix reads both locations, converts once at the page door with z.toJSONSchema, uses structuredClone as the pre-check it literally is, and reports per-tool what the browser ACCEPTED rather than what was attempted.

Fixing discovery then exposed what the page says ABOUT agents. Presence meant 'a WebMCP binding exists in this tab', so an agent working the same map over /api/mcp was invisible - the header said 'No agent attached' while that agent wrote nodes onto the board. Presence now reads off the exchange log, the one thing every door writes to, with a 90-second window: a binding proves an agent CAN act, a recent agent event proves one IS acting. And AgentHandoff returning null the moment WebMCP bound was its own bug - WebMCP is pull-only, so binding makes a map REACHABLE, not worked; the page hit its most capable state and showed nothing to act on while an attached agent sat beside it with the whole catalog and no instruction.

WHAT THIS CYCLE ADDED ON TOP OF THE PROTOTYPE. Two extractions, both earning their place: useDismissOnOutside, which deduplicated three hand-rolled copies of the same outside-click-plus-Escape effect (AgentStatus, BoardMenu, BriefMenu) and now has 8 tests of its own; and AgentStatusPanel split into AgentStatusNarrative / AgentToolChips / AgentBindDiagnostics, because it was answering three different questions - what presence means in prose, which tools got through, and the build-time detail behind both - and the diagnostics half now owns its own NODE_ENV gate so the panel is a plain composition.

The prototype had shipped four library functions with no tests of their own: attachedStartCopy, jsonSchemaFor, onModelContextReady, and requestUserInteraction. Rather than register a testFile satisfier pointing at a file that did not actually exercise them, this cycle wrote the missing tests - 20 of the 27 registered - including the late-injection race onModelContextReady exists for, the bounded 30-second watch, and the ignore-a-ready-event-with-no-agent-behind-it case that would otherwise bind against nothing and report a connection that does not exist.

SCOPE VERDICT. Against the project's deliverables: all 9 build-track deliverables were already resolved as delivered before this cycle and this cycle deferred none of them; the 10th (registering the MCP server in a client such as Claude Desktop) remains deferred to the assist track, and that deferral is recorded decidedBy user at the plan gate, not an agent decision. Against this feature's own plan, delivered in full: discovery fixed, schemas converted, failures reported, presence unified across doors, the start cue added, the header reduced to one line with detail behind a click, and WebMcpDiagnostics deleted with zero dangling references. 24 scenarios registered - 23 component plus one new application scenario, 'The agent worked here, then left', which seeds agent events with an explicit hours-old createdAt so the 90-second window closes and the page honestly reports absence over an agent's own visible work. That state is the direct counterpart to 'Mid-exchange', which now reads 'Agent attached' in a capture iframe where WebMCP cannot bind - the exact lie this feature set out to end, now demonstrable.

RESOLVES A PRIOR DEFERRAL. The previous cycle deferred 'AgentStatus renders 1 tools' - the headline interpolated tools.length with no pluralisation. That is moot rather than fixed: the count left the header entirely and became a named chip list in AgentToolChips, where names rather than a number are the point, because as a count a shortfall reads like a rounding difference.

RECORDED N-A. WebMcpBridge's 'many' archetype resolves to registered=many, and that component mounts the real bridge, which reads acceptance off a live WebMCP binding. A capture runs in an iframe and WebMCP is top-level-secure-context only, so registered is structurally always empty there; no seed or fixture can change it without replacing the component under test. The state is demonstrated where it can be staged honestly as props: AgentToolChips - AllNine, AgentStatusPanel - BoundToPage, AgentStatus - PanelOpen.

OPERATIONAL NOTE, recorded because it cost real time and was self-inflicted. A project-wide recapture launched mid-session drove the same dev server the Live Preview renders through, and the preview stopped responding twice. Diagnosis found the machine genuinely resource-starved - 16 GB with ~200 MB free, 4 GB of 5 GB swap used, load average 173 on 8 cores - and, underneath that, an ORPHANED vitest parent process respawning workers in a loop, retriggered by the recapture writing 100+ screenshot files. Killing it took load from 173 to 102, and a dev-server restart plus letting it settle brought it to 3.4. The lesson for future cycles: a full recapture is a foreground-blocking operation from the user's point of view even when backgrounded, and it belongs at the commit step or behind an explicit ask, not opportunistically mid-session.
